title: Is Chess a City or a Battlefield?
body: Long ago, a monk named Jacobus de Cessolis claimed that a chessboard was actually a miniature model of a bustling city. He imagined the different pieces as citizens working together. Years later, the famous Spanish master Ruy Lopez disagreed, saying the board is actually a fierce battlefield where two royal armies clash.

variants.lucy: A monk named Jacobus looked at the wooden board and saw a quiet, busy town. He imagined the little pieces as neighbors, like bakers and builders, all helping each other live in peace. To him, every square was a tiny street where people worked side by side.
variants.luca: But then a Spanish champion named Ruy Lopez charged in with a totally different plan! He declared that those sixty-four squares were actually a wild, daring battlefield. For him, the game was a thrilling clash between two noble forces fighting for victory.
variants.cn: 有一位修士叫雅各布斯，他看着木头棋盘，看到的却是一座安静又热闹的小城。在他的想象里，小小的棋子就像住在一起的邻居——有面包师，有建筑工，大家互相帮忙，和和气气地过日子。在他眼里，每一个方格都是一条小小的街道，人们在那里肩并肩地干活。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

titleCn: 国际象棋是城市还是战场？
